content.text: OnPush doesn't watch your inputs. It's a dirty flag: a change detection pass checks an OnPush component only if something marked it, and four things do: Angular setting an input to a new value, an event handled in the component or below it, a change to a signal its template reads, and
. Writing an input property from your own code marks nothing.
An Angular 22 app opens an upload dialog with
and pushes each progress value into the dialog's
input. The dialog shows 0% and stays there until the upload finishes and it closes. A log in the subscription prints 10, 20, 30 up to 100, and
holds each value. "I'm changing its input," the developer says, "and OnPush updates when inputs change."
The belief: an OnPush component updates when, and only when, one of its input references changes. Change an input, it re-renders; leave the inputs alone, it never will.

It's how OnPush was taught for years, usually as "OnPush plus immutable inputs", and the most famous OnPush bug seems to confirm it: push an item into an array you passed to an OnPush child and the child doesn't update, because the reference didn't change. The rule has two halves, and both are off. Inputs aren't watched at all; Angular marks the component when it sets one itself. And inputs are only one of four triggers, the only one that comes from the parent. In Angular 22, where every component is OnPush unless it says otherwise, the difference shows up everywhere.

Marks travel up, skips travel down
When an event fires in a component, Angular marks that component and every ancestor up to the root, because a pass can only reach a view through its parents. The docs' example: a click in an OnPush

checked, since the child is part of the parent's view. That has a cost. A keystroke in a small filter box nested inside a heavy OnPush grid re-evaluates the grid's whole template on every key. Signals are the precise trigger: Angular refreshes the component whose template read the signal and only walks through its OnPush ancestors to reach it, without re-evaluating their templates.

Skipping works the other way: when a pass skips an OnPush component, it skips its whole subtree. The API docs put it plainly: the OnPush strategy applies to all child directives and cannot be overridden.
